title: Animals: Wild Wonders
description: Speed, size, and survival—remarkable creatures in five facts.

questions.question: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.hint: Spotted cat that can sprint 70 mph
questions.explanation: Cheetahs can't roar like lions. Instead they purr and chirp like birds, and a cheetah's chirp can be heard a mile away!

questions.question: Cheetahs can accelerate to 60 mph in about how many seconds?
questions.explanation: That's as quick as a sports car! At full speed, each cheetah stride stretches about 23 feet, and it takes four of those strides every second.

questions.question: Cheetahs hit 60 mph in about three seconds and hold the speed record. Which animal holds the size record as the biggest that has ever lived?
questions.hint: An ocean giant bigger than any dinosaur
questions.explanation: Blue whales can grow more than 100 feet long, bigger than any dinosaur! A blue whale's tongue alone can weigh as much as an elephant.

questions.question: The giant blue whale eats some of the tiniest food in the sea. What are these shrimplike creatures called?
questions.explanation: A blue whale can gulp about 16 tons of krill in a single day. All that krill turns its poop bright orange-pink!

questions.question: Some black-and-white Antarctic birds eat so much krill that their poop turns pink! Which birds are they?
questions.explanation: Adélie penguin colonies leave pink poop stains so big that scientists can spot them from space! The color even tells them whether the penguins ate krill or fish.
